issue_summary: A substantial portion of interaction records designated as campaign-driven—specifically Email Open, Email Click, and Event Attendance—are missing their associated campaign identifier. While organic and relationship manager interactions are permitted to have null campaign identifiers, interactions explicitly driven by marketing activities require campaign attribution to accurately associate customer touchpoints with specific campaigns.

observed_evidence.description: Missing campaign_id among campaign-driven interaction types only. Eligible types: ['Email Open', 'Email Click', 'Event Attendance']. Organic / RM interactions with NULL campaign_id are not counted. FAIL when missing attribution rate > 0.08.

business_impact: Implication: Marketing effectiveness and attribution reporting may significantly undercount engagement generated by marketing initiatives. Commercial banking business teams and marketing leaders risk misallocating campaign budgets or misjudging customer interest due to skewed return on marketing investment analyses and incomplete touchpoint tracking.

possible_root_causes.hypothesis: Marketing automation and event tracking source systems may fail to pass the campaign identifier payload during webhook or event ingestion when tracking pixels or redirect links lack UTM or campaign parameters.
possible_root_causes.verification_step: Query raw ingestion logs from the marketing automation and event platforms to verify whether incoming interaction payloads contain campaign identifiers before entering the transformation layer.

possible_root_causes.hypothesis: Upstream ETL transformation logic or join operations against campaign reference tables may drop or overwrite campaign identifiers when matching interaction keys to the campaign master table.
possible_root_causes.verification_step: Review the interaction pipeline code and execution logs to check join conditions and transformations between raw interaction events and the campaign dimension table.

possible_root_causes.hypothesis: Certain event management tools or email service provider configurations might record attendance or email interactions without enforcing campaign assignment at creation time.
possible_root_causes.verification_step: Inspect source system configuration and interaction schemas across distinct platforms (e.g., event portal vs. email tool) broken down by interaction type to determine if missing identifiers correlate with specific delivery channels.

recommended_investigation_steps: Group the affected interaction records missing campaign attribution by interaction type, source system, and event date to identify any clustering or channel-specific patterns.
Review the upstream ingestion pipelines and API payloads connecting email and event platforms to the interactions dataset to identify where the campaign identifier is lost.
Inspect the data transformation scripts and lookup logic that map raw campaign codes or tracking tags to the campaign identifier in the interactions table.
recommended_remediation: Implement validation rules at the ingestion boundary to reject or quarantine campaign-driven interaction events that arrive without a valid campaign identifier.
Update marketing platform tagging standards and automated link builders to enforce mandatory campaign identifier parameters in email templates and event registration portals.
Backfill missing campaign identifiers where deterministic linkage is possible using related event metadata, delivery logs, or timestamp proximity to known campaign distributions.
limitations: This assessment is based solely on a validated data quality finding from synthetic commercial banking data. Direct access to live banking environments, upstream marketing platforms, event ingestion pipelines, and raw source log files is not available; therefore, all suggested causes are hypotheses requiring empirical verification by the data engineering team.
